newsitem.title: UK: Government plans regeneration of former coalfields.
newsitem.headline: Government plans regeneration of former coalfields.

text.p: The British government said on Wednesday that the ownership of around 80 disused coalfields was being transferred from the state to the English Partnerships agency, which would oversee a wide-ranging regeneration project.
The properties concerned are in north and central England and belong to state-owned British Coal. The government has sold off the remaining working pits to the private sector.
English Partnerships, a government development agency, plans to invest 300 million pounds ($495 million) to reclaim the sites and hopes to attract some 850 million pounds of private investment.

The Department of the Environment said some 2,250 acres (910 hectares) of land will be reclaimed for residential, commercial and retail use, and 2,750 acres (1,113 hectares) for forestry, agriculture and leisure.
The government believes that 55,000 jobs could be created through the project.
